final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the existing record more narrowly. That clarification is legitimate but not outcome-determinative. The existing evidence still supports two distinct propositions: first, general launch readiness has some support because the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.4 points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents; second, policy compliance for certification remains unresolved because the field-service dispatch segment misses target, is a named launch use case tied to enterprise commitments, legal review on disclosure is still open, and the release policy requires disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case. Public risk-management and model-card guidance support monitoring and documentation posture, but they do not satisfy that specific policy predicate. This is why the case is not `compliant_with_caveats`: the caveat here is not merely descriptive or prudential; it is an unresolved compliance condition required by policy. On the present record, the certification rationale remains evidentially supported only in a bounded readiness sense and not affirmatively supported as policy-compliant launch certification.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows disclosure of the dispatch-segment limitation in the model card or launch materials.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering the named launch use-case limitation before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the dispatch-segment performance gap was resolved at launch threshold.
Legal review remains open on whether disclosure is required, leaving a policy predicate unresolved.
The affected segment is named in two enterprise deployment commitments, so non-core or low-volume framing does not resolve materiality under the policy text.
